question.html:
Relative velocity of two objects in free fall. Two particles are released from rest in a region of space where the acceleration due to gravity is uniform. Particle A is released at time and particle B is released at a later time . During the interval when both particles are in motion and air resistance is neglected, how does the magnitude of the velocity of particle A relative to particle B behave?

  1. It is zero at all times
  2. It remains constant and non-zero
  3. It increases linearly with time
  4. It increases as the square of the time elapsed
